common_name: Ground Hug Aronia (Dwarf Groundcover Black Chokeberry)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring as a dense, weed-suppressing groundcover, slope stabilizer, or low edging; space closer together for a solid mat within two seasons.

directions: Ground Hug is a University of Connecticut-bred dwarf selection of black chokeberry, part of the Proven Winners Low Scape series, prized for a mat-forming habit under 14 inches tall that spreads gently rather than suckering aggressively into thickets like the wild species. It carries the same white spring flower clusters and small glossy black berries as full-size Aronia melanocarpa, plus vivid red-orange fall foliage, all on a scale suited to groundcover use. The shrub tolerates wet, dry, clay, and salt-affected soils with ease, making it a practical choice for parking-lot islands, slopes, and mass plantings where mowing is impractical. Beyond an occasional light shearing to keep the mat even, it needs no routine pruning.

common_name: Low Scape Snowfire Chokeberry (Heavy-Blooming Dwarf Black Chokeberry)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in a mixed border, mass planting, or roadside bed; this compact selection needs no pollinator and blooms heavily its first full season.

directions: Low Scape Snowfire is a Proven Winners selection of black chokeberry bred as the heaviest-flowering plant in the Low Scape series, blanketing its low mounded form in white spring blossoms that draw a steady stream of pollinators before setting a heavy crop of dark blue-black berries. The compact, spreading habit tops out around two feet, with glossy dark green summer foliage that turns deep red and purple in fall. It accepts clay, alkaline, wet, or drought-stressed soils with equal ease and tolerates road salt, making it a practical choice for roadside plantings, coastal landscapes, or mass groundcover use. Beyond an occasional light shearing to maintain a neat mound, the shrub requires no routine maintenance.
